summary: Task 17.1 (bounded diagnostics metrics model + instrumentation) meets its acceptance criteria. The new src/ArrTags/Diagnostics model exposes exactly the ADR-025 clause 3 counter set (queue depth/in-flight, per-provider connection health, matching failures by bounded classification, cache hits/misses, render failures by bounded classification, stale-metadata transitions) with a fixed shape; every member type is an int/long count, a bounded enum, or one of the two fixed count records, with no string/path/item identity/provider payload/credential/SecretLease/array/collection member (inspected in the model source, not only the tests). Instrumentation is placed at existing bounded boundaries (inventory-cache decision in the Radarr/Sonarr readers; read outcome in ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader; match status and fresh-to-stale write in MetadataReconciliationProcessor; RenderFailed result in ArtworkGenerationCoordinator) and uses process-lifetime Interlocked/Volatile counters; no queue, coalescing, cache, configuration, save-path, endpoint, route, page, or dependency change was introduced. GetSnapshot() reads only in-memory counters and the existing lock-protected LibraryWorkQueue.Count/InFlightCount, performs no provider/render/library/I-O work, and is DI-resolvable. Build is 0 warnings / 0 errors and the default suite is Failed 0 / Passed 1780 / Skipped 63 / Total 1843, i.e. +24 passed / +24 total versus the 1819 baseline with no new skips (the two new files contain 24 cases and no Skip). Documentation/state (changelog, PLANS.md checkbox, state.json done/reports/updated_utc) is reconciled; phase 17 remains PLANNED and no gate/tag was applied. No blocking issues found.

findings.summary: The DI test resolves only DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider, not the readers/decorator/processor, so it does not directly assert that DiagnosticsMetrics is injected into the instrumented production graph.
findings.detail: DiagnosticsSnapshotTests.SnapshotProviderIsResolvableFromTheRegistratorWithoutProviderWork builds the real RegisterServices provider and resolves DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider (requires LibraryWorkQueue + DiagnosticsMetrics), which proves the provider is resolvable. It does not resolve RadarrMetadataReader/SonarrMetadataReader/ConcurrencyLimitedArrMetadataReader<T>/MetadataReconciliationProcessor to assert their private _metrics field is the shared singleton. This is covered by established container behavior plus existing project evidence: the same constructors already rely on optional registered parameters (ArrInventoryCacheProvider? inventory, IArrTagsLog<T>? log), and the ADR-018 inventory cache functions in production only because the container injects those optional services. Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection injects a registered service into an optional parameter (and uses the default only when the service is unregistered). No behavioral gap is present; a direct assertion would strengthen regression evidence only. Not required for 17.1.
findings.recommended_action: Optionally add a DI-resolution assertion for the reader/decorator/processor _metrics field in a future task; not required for 17.1 acceptance.

findings.summary: Provider health reflects the last observed reconciliation-read outcome, not a scheduled probe; never-observed and unclassifiable both report Unknown.
findings.detail: The recorded value is Healthy on a successful read and ArrConnectionHealthMapping.FromErrorCode(error.Code) on a failed read, held in two slots bounded by ArrProviderKind. A provider that has never been read (or is disabled) reports Unknown, the same value an unclassified error maps to. No production code consumes ArrProviderClient.ProbeAsync, and ArrConnectionCatalog always constructs health as Unknown, so this read-outcome source is the only meaningful bounded source available. ADR-025 clause 3 requires bounded provider connection health, which is satisfied; the ambiguity is disclosed in the worker report known_limitations. Not a defect for 17.1.
findings.recommended_action: None for 17.1; a scheduled probe or explicit never-observed state would require a new decision and is out of scope.

findings.summary: RenderFailureCounts uses an 18-argument positional constructor coupled to RenderFailureReason declaration order; the pinning test detects gaps/name drift but not a same-cardinality reorder of enum members.
findings.detail: DiagnosticsMetrics.CreateRenderFailureCounts passes ReadRenderFailure(reason) arguments in current enum order and the constructor assigns them positionally. DiagnosticsSnapshotTests.RenderFailureCountsExposeOneCountPerDeclaredReason asserts numeric contiguity and that the property-name set equals the enum-name set, which catches a gap or an added/removed reason but would not catch two members swapping positions while remaining contiguous. This is a latent future-maintenance risk, not a present correctness issue given the frozen enum, and the enum is documented as a bounded whole. The classification exposed is bounded and correct today.
findings.recommended_action: No change required for 17.1; a future value-keyed mapping would be more robust if the enum ever grows/reorders.

criterion_verification.criterion: GetSnapshot() is thread-safe, performs no provider/render/library/I-O work, and is DI-resolvable (17.2 will consume it).
criterion_verification.evidence: DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider.GetSnapshot() = _metrics.Capture(_queue.Count, _queue.InFlightCount); LibraryWorkQueue.Count/InFlightCount are in-memory lock-protected ints (LibraryWorkQueue.cs:84-107). Capture copies Interlocked.Read counters and Volatile two health slots and allocates only the snapshot. Registration uses TryAddSingleton<DiagnosticsMetrics>() and a factory-backed TryAddSingleton<DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider>; DiagnosticsSnapshotTests.SnapshotProviderIsResolvableFromTheRegistratorWithoutProviderWork resolves it from the real registrator and reads an all-zero snapshot. CountersAreThreadSafeAndReportExactTotals runs 4096 concurrent increments of every path and asserts exact totals.
